- [nsw.gov.au](https://www.nsw.gov.au/driving-boating-and-transport/vehicle-registration/fees-concessions-and-forms/vehicle-registration-fees)
- [revenue.nsw.gov.au](https://www.revenue.nsw.gov.au/taxes-duties-levies-royalties/motor-vehicle-duty)
- [sira.nsw.gov.au](https://www.sira.nsw.gov.au/motor/compulsory-third-party-motor-vehicle-insurance-green-slips/how-prices-are-set)
- [vicroads.vic.gov.au](https://www.vicroads.vic.gov.au/registrations/new-registrations/register-vehicle-from-another-state)
- [sro.vic.gov.au](https://www.sro.vic.gov.au/motor-vehicle-duty-current-rates)
- [tac.vic.gov.au](https://www.tac.vic.gov.au/about-the-tac/our-organisation/transport-accident-charge)

faqs.q: How long do I have to register my car after moving across the NSW and Victorian border?
faqs.a: Neither regulator publishes the grace period people expect. Service NSW states that a vehicle kept or garaged in NSW without NSW registration is considered unregistered, which makes the effective deadline immediate. Victoria sets no day count either, but ties a real consequence to a date: if your interstate registration expired more than three months before your VicRoads appointment, you lose the roadworthy waiver and must buy a Victorian certificate of roadworthiness.

faqs.q: Do I need a NSW blue slip if my Victorian registration is still current?
faqs.a: Yes. Transport for NSW lists a vehicle brought into NSW from another state or territory as one of the circumstances that requires an Authorised Unregistered Vehicle Inspection Scheme report. Current Victorian registration makes no difference to that. The maximum fee for a light vehicle is $82 including GST as at 1 July 2026, and the report is valid for 42 days, so book it close to your Service NSW visit rather than months ahead.

faqs.q: Will I pay stamp duty twice if I move my own car across the border?
faqs.a: No. Both states exempt a vehicle that keeps the same owner. Revenue NSW exempts a vehicle registered in your name in another state or territory on which duty has already been paid, and you prove it with the current interstate certificate of registration. Victoria exempts a vehicle registered in the same name as its previous interstate registration, provided the Commissioner is satisfied the interstate registration was not made to avoid Victorian duty.

faqs.q: Is the Victorian TAC charge the same thing as a NSW green slip?
faqs.a: They do the same job and are priced in opposite ways. A NSW green slip is a separate policy you buy from a licensed insurer before registering, and insurers rate it on factors including your age, driving history, demerit points, claims history and where the car is parked. Victoria's TAC charge sits inside the registration bill and is set only by vehicle class and the garaging postcode. Your driving record does not affect it.

faqs.q: Can I use a Wodonga roadworthy certificate for my Albury pink slip?
faqs.a: No. Transport for NSW accepts an interstate inspection report only if you are more than 50 kilometres from the NSW border. Albury, Corowa, Mulwala, Tocumwal and Moama all sit inside that radius, so the concession that exists for distant motorists is unavailable to the towns closest to Victoria. Your annual safety inspection has to be done at an authorised inspection station on the NSW side of the river.

faqs.q: What registration refund do I get when I leave the state?
faqs.a: Leaving NSW, only the motor vehicle tax is refundable. The registration fee and the number plate fee are not, and Service NSW allows six to eight weeks to process form 1565. Leaving Victoria, the refund covers the time left on the registration, less a $22.10 processing fee and 10 per cent of the TAC charge, paid within ten business days. If the balance is smaller than those deductions, nothing is paid.

faqs.q: Do I get my green slip money back if I move to Victoria?
faqs.a: Probably not. SIRA lists partial CTP refund eligibility for vehicles that have been written off, taken to an auto wrecker, or stolen. A move interstate is not on that list, and a sold vehicle is expressly excluded because the policy attaches to the car rather than the owner. Ask your insurer directly, since an administration fee may also be deducted, and where possible time the move near your green slip expiry.

faqs.q: Do I have to hand in my old interstate number plates?
faqs.a: Yes, in both directions. Service NSW asks for the original interstate plates when you lodge the registration application, and VicRoads takes the interstate plates at your appointment and issues a receipt for them. Service NSW notes that a small number of interstate plate types can be retained, depending on the issuing state. Budget $58 for NSW plates or $44.20 for a Victorian pair, and take a screwdriver to VicRoads.
